title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why does the module say pedagogical quality is irrelevant to mandated-training compliance? `[V]`
options: Because regulators do not evaluate training quality in any form
Because statutes specify duration, interactivity, and content elements — so a course can be excellent, accurate, and still omit a required element, and the audit gives no partial credit for quality
Because quality standards vary too much between jurisdictions to be enforceable
Because compliance training is exempt from instructional design standards
questions.explanation: It is Module 3's jurisdictional drift with a penalty attached: nothing in the content is untrue, every fact checks out, and the obligation isn't satisfied.

questions.prompt: What is the correct current statement of the EU position for a learning function? `[V]`
options: The entire AI Act regime was deferred to December 2027, so nothing binds until then

High-risk employment obligations moved to 2 December 2027, but AI literacy and the emotion-recognition prohibition have bound since February 2025 and the transparency obligations since 2 August 2026 — which puts a learning chatbot in scope now
All obligations took effect on 2 August 2026 as originally scheduled
The Act applies only to systems that make automated employment decisions
questions.explanation: Deferral of one regime isn't runway across the Act. A learner who takes away only the 2027 date has the dangerous version of this lesson.

questions.prompt: Why does the module treat accessibility as a volume problem specifically?
options: Because larger organizations face more litigation risk
Because each failure is per-asset with a small fixed remediation cost, so exposure scales linearly with how much you publish — and concentrates in the cheap-to-produce material nobody reviewed
Because AI-generated content is inherently less accessible than human-authored content
Because WCAG conformance must be recertified as catalogs grow
questions.explanation: A function that went from twelve modules to sixty didn't triple its risk. And the material at highest volume is the least reviewed, which is where the debt sits.

questions.prompt: Which is the most common accessibility failure in AI-generated learning media? `[V]`
options: Reading level above the target audience
Insufficient time allowed to complete assessments
Generated video arriving without captions or a transcript, because text-to-video produces video rather than captioned video
Navigation structures that are too deeply nested
questions.explanation: It arrives by default rather than by oversight, which is what makes it the reliable one. The fix is a requirement in the brief, not a review step.

questions.prompt: When does a skills taxonomy become a decision system?
options: When it is used by more than one function
When the inference is generated by a machine-learning model rather than entered manually
When an allocation of opportunity depends on the inference — the tell is what happens downstream of the output, not what the system outputs
When it contains protected-characteristic data
questions.explanation: Nobody experiences building a taxonomy as building a decision engine, which is why 101 M7's line has never been pointed here. B is a distractor: a manually maintained taxonomy that gates a succession slate is the same problem.

questions.prompt: What is the boundary between this role and the People Analytics specialism on skills inference?
options: People Analytics owns the technology and L&D owns the change management
People Analytics owns whether the inference is any good; this role owns what happens to a person because of it
People Analytics owns internal systems and L&D owns vendor systems
There is no boundary — the two disciplines have identical responsibilities here
questions.explanation: Both questions need answering and they are genuinely different. Validity is one discipline's craft; consequence is the other's.

questions.prompt: What does the module say about content-library licences and AI ingestion? `[V]`
options: Standard enterprise licences generally permit ingestion for internal adaptation
Most licences predate generative AI and grant a right to deliver content, leaving ingestion for summarization or derivative generation unaddressed — which is not the same as permitted
Ingestion is permitted provided the derivative work is not distributed externally
Copyright law resolves this independently of the licence terms
questions.explanation: The gap is silence rather than permission, and silence is where organizations assume in their own favour. It is a question to ask before you need the answer.

questions.prompt: A learner reports their organization has no accessibility standard for learning content at all. How should that be treated?
options: As a reason to skip the accessibility section of the activity
As a finding more serious than a failure rate, which belongs in the write-up and should be scored as one
As acceptable where the organization is below the relevant headcount threshold
As a matter for the IT function rather than L&D
questions.explanation: A pass rate tells you how you're doing against a standard. No standard means nobody has ever asked, and every asset published since is unexamined, which is a larger fact about the function than any percentage.
